newsitem.title: USA: McDonnell Douglas June 30 backlog down.
newsitem.headline: McDonnell Douglas June 30 backlog down.

text.p: McDonnell Douglas Corp said Thursday it had firm backlog of $21.9 billion on June 30, down from $23.7 billion on December 31.
Total backlog was $42.2 billion on June 30, down from $44.4 billion on December 31.

Earlier, McDonnell Douglas reported second quarter earnings of $0.93 a share, up from $0.87 a year ago. Costs related to merger activities in the second quarter were offset by a favorable resolution of state tax issues, McDonnell said.
McDonnell has agreed to merge with aircraft maker Boeing Co.

"Solid financial results for the second quarter of 1997 are gratifying," Harry Stonecipher, president, said in a statement. "I am pleased to see that we kept our eye on the ball and did not let the merger distract us from running our business."
McDonnell's second quarter revenues rose to $3.6 billion from $3.3 billion, with all segments showing increases. The laregest gain was in the military aircraft segment.

Military aircraft operating earnings fell to $238 million from $243 million. Improved earnings in the C-17 cargo and F-15 fighter programs largely offset lower earnings in the F/A-18 program. Military revenues were $2.1 billion, up from $1.9 billion.
Missiles, space and electronic systems earnings fell to $45 million from $53 million. Sales were $587 million, up from $529 million.
Commercial aircraft earnings fell to $14 million from $18 million in the second quarter. Revenues were $805 million, up from $722 million a year ago.
Within the commercial aircraft segment, earnings from the sale of spare parts and related services were largely offset by losses from development activities and sale of production aircraft.
Interest expense totaled $21 milion in the second quarter, down from $31 million in the year-ago quarter.
